newsitem.title: BELGIUM: British EU commissioners block avoparcin ban.
newsitem.headline: British EU commissioners block avoparcin ban.

text.p: A proposed European Union ban on the drug avoparcin has been blocked by the European Commission's two British Commissioners, a senior Commission official said.
Avoparcin, manufactured by Roche UK, part of Roche Holding AG Holdings AG, is used as a growth enhancer by pig and poultry producers to aid feed efficiency.

Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler proposed in December to ban the drug which is not permitted in Denmark and Germany after the EU standing veterinary committee supported concerns that the drug could lead to resistance to antibiotics in humans.
But, both Britain's senior commissioner Sir Leon Brittan and Neil Kinnock blocked adoption of the ban by written procedure.
They have asked for more scientific evidence to support the proposal.
"The proposed ban has been blocked by two Commissioners and the Commission is now preparing more evidence," the official said.
The Commisson is confident that the ban can be adopted before April 1 when the proposal says it should come into force.
"If it cannot be adopted by written proceedure it may have to be put to a meeting of the Commission for a decision," the official said.
